clue.text: Mixture of chicken and dog

blocks.note: a cock is a male chicken
to dog someone is to follow them closely, to tail them

explanation.surface: A mongrel crossbreed of a hen and a hound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' is a verb here, meaning to shadow someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail is a drink blended from several ingredients, hence any mixed combination.

clue.text: Production of offspring is very simple

definitions.note: an adjective phrase; the answer is a noun, as in 'it's child's play'

blocks.note: cryptically, a stage production put on by a youngster
the idiom for a task that is no trouble at all

explanation.surface: Having children is easy, the clue cheekily claims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Production' looks biological; it is a theatrical show.
explanation.definitionFit: Child's play is an idiom for anything so easy a youngster could manage it.

clue.text: Talk about smart French wine is biased

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps the pieces that follow

blocks.note: to chat is to talk
U means upper-class, hence smart
vin is French for wine
taken as written

explanation.surface: Snobbish remarks about a trendy French wine are prejudiced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' looks like the link to the definition but belongs in the wordplay. U for upper-class is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A chauvinist attitude is one of excessive, prejudiced loyalty to one's own group or sex.

clue.text: Whole lotta' shakin' goin' on!

indicators.note: shaking something jumbles its contents, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: The title of the Jerry Lee Lewis rock and roll hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Total as an adjective means complete or entire, the same as whole.

clue.text: Fashionable workplace where MPs have all the answers!

definitions.text: where MPs have all the answers

blocks.note: in means fashionable
read as work + place: op, short for opus, is a work, and a position is a place

explanation.surface: A trendy office where politicians know everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workplace' reads as one word but splits in two. The joke is that MPs out of power always claim to know better than the government.
explanation.definitionFit: Parties not in government sit in opposition, where criticism is easy and solutions cost nothing.

clue.text: I breathe extremely fresh air in Spain and Portugal

indicators.note: at the extremes of a word means at its two ends, so only its outermost letters are kept
something made fresh is made new, so these letters are given a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the first and last letters of breathe
the letters of air rearranged

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker enjoying the clean air of the Iberian countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberia is the name of the peninsula that the two countries Spain and Portugal share.

clue.text: Board game where ball goes round opening to get a point

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so one word is wrapped around another

blocks.note: taken as written
a gate is an opening in a fence or wall
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A table game in which a ball circles a hole to score.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagatelle is a game played on a board where balls are struck into numbered holes.

clue.text: I run into disaster

indicators.note: turning into something means changing form, so these letters change their order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone heading straight for catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin is a state of collapse or destruction, a synonym of disaster or downfall.

clue.text: Soldiers give guns to Yugoslav leader

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: to arm is to supply with weapons
the opening letter of Yugoslav

explanation.surface: Troops supplying weapons to the head of Yugoslavia.
explanation.definitionFit: An army is a large organised body of soldiers, so the plural noun matches it collectively.

clue.text: Idleness is surrounded by endeavour

blocks.note: to be in something is to be surrounded by it
an endeavour is an action undertaken

explanation.surface: A paradox: laziness hemmed in on all sides by effort.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a container, but the pieces simply sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Inaction is the state of doing nothing at all, which is what idleness amounts to.

clue.text: Selfishness resulting when one is confused with some Godhead

indicators.note: things confused are jumbled up, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
read as God's head: the first letter of God

explanation.surface: Thinking yourself divine is a sure route to self-absorption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Godhead' reads as one word, but it splits: the head of God.
explanation.definitionFit: Egoism is putting your own interests first, a close synonym of selfishness.

clue.text: Consequence of secure prison break

indicators.note: breaking something smashes it into pieces that reassemble differently

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: The fallout after inmates escape a high-security jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A repercussion is an unintended effect or result following an action, especially an unwelcome one.

clue.text: Progress in review of Devon temple

indicators.note: a review looks over material again and reworks it, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: both words are the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: An inspector reports on the building work at a church in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Development is growth or advancement over time, which is a sense of the noun progress.

clue.text: Angling round Flamborough Head and East Riding primarily for kids' food

indicators.note: a head is the top, so the first letter of the place name is taken
round means encircling, so the first word wraps around the next piece
primarily means first of all, so the opening letters of these words are kept

blocks.note: angling is fishing with a rod
the first letter of Flamborough
the first letters of East and Riding

explanation.surface: Fishing off Flamborough Head on the Yorkshire coast to feed the children.
explanation.walkthrough: Flamborough Head is a headland on the East Riding of Yorkshire coast; here 'Head' picks a letter. A fish finger is a breaded fish stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish fingers are breaded strips of fish, a staple British children's meal.

clue.text: Unfaithful partners took time to meet last month, hesitating twice on 1st September

indicators.note: the 1st of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: AD, anno domini, marks a period of time
ult., ultimo, is the abbreviation for last month in formal letters
er is a sound of hesitation, used twice
the opening letter of September

explanation.surface: A pair of cheating lovers met up last month in early September.
explanation.walkthrough: ULT (ultimo) is old business-letter shorthand for last month.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulterers are married people who are sexually unfaithful to their spouses, unfaithful partners.

clue.text: Police car used in stop and arrest operation

indicators.note: the answer is put to use inside the following words, lying within them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of stop, all of and, and the start of arrest

explanation.surface: A patrol vehicle deployed in a stop-and-search style police raid.
explanation.walkthrough: A panda car is a British name for a small police patrol car, once painted in black and white panels.
explanation.definitionFit: Panda is short for panda car, the British nickname for a police patrol vehicle.

clue.text: Earthborn, perhaps, but disgusting!

indicators.note: perhaps hints the word is only one possible arrangement of these letters

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A mortal creature of the earth, yet repellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Abhorrent means inspiring loathing or revulsion, a strong synonym of disgusting.

clue.text: Enchant for a time, then bore

blocks.note: a spell is a period of time
a bind is a tedious nuisance, something that bores

explanation.surface: Someone charming at first who then turns tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: A bind is British slang for a tiresome chore.
explanation.definitionFit: To spellbind is to hold someone fascinated as if under magic, which is to enchant them.

clue.text: The Oriental cat is amazingly sensitive to beautiful things

indicators.note: something amazing leaves things in a whirl, so the preceding letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
E for East, the Orient
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Siamese cat shows a remarkable eye for lovely objects.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesthetic as an adjective describes appreciation of beauty and art, a taste for the lovely.

clue.text: She introduces the English to the Spanish

indicators.note: to introduce one thing to another is to bring it inside, so the first piece goes within the second

blocks.note: the English word for the definite article
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A hostess presenting English guests to Spanish ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' stands for any woman, so a woman's name fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethel is a female given name, and a woman can be referred to by the pronoun she.

clue.text: Fell over on duty at hotel facility

indicators.note: turned over means flipped end to end, so the word before is read backwards

blocks.note: a fell is upland moorland in northern England
being on duty is being in service

explanation.surface: A hotel worker tripped up while working a shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like the past tense of fall; it is the noun for a hill or moor.
explanation.definitionFit: Room service is a hotel's arrangement for delivering meals and drinks to guests' bedrooms.

clue.text: Roman Catholic takes prophet in to see holy remains

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: RC is the abbreviation for Roman Catholic
Eli is a prophet and priest in the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A Catholic brings a holy man along to view sacred relics.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is a body part or belonging of a saint kept and venerated as holy.

clue.text: Unhappy owls are sluggish

indicators.note: unhappy means not content or settled, so these letters are not left in their order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Miserable birds of prey are lethargic.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow means moving without speed or energy, like something sluggish and torpid.

clue.text: Remove nitrogen from salt water to make French cheese

indicators.note: removing means taking out, so a letter goes from the word named

blocks.note: brine is salty water
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen; this letter is taken away

explanation.surface: A chemistry recipe: purify seawater to produce cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft white-rinded cheese named after a region east of Paris.

clue.text: Cool room for fat Queen

blocks.note: lard is pig fat
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A chilled chamber set aside for a portly monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A larder is a cool storeroom or pantry where food is kept fresh.

clue.text: Diana has a record, we are told, of the conversation

indicators.note: what we are told reaches us by ear, so the words are judged by their sound

blocks.note: Di is short for Diana and a log is a record; 'has' only joins them

explanation.surface: Diana has kept minutes of a discussion, so we hear.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialogue is an exchange of speech between two or more people, a talk.

clue.text: The war upset the band

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A pop group falls out over a conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests musicians, but here it is a ring or circlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreath is a ring of flowers or leaves, a circular band worn or hung up.

clue.text: University growth's resulting in fantastic things!

blocks.note: uni is the short form of university
a corn is a hard growth on the foot; the possessive is read as a plural

explanation.surface: A campus expansion producing marvellous results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' means of fantasy here, not wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Unicorns are mythical horned horses, creatures belonging to fantasy and legend.
